text:
penny: noticing odd behavior across SDKs for SSE streaming. JS SDK tolerates a stray LF and recovers, python-sdk raises JSON parse error, go-sdk sometimes emits messages out of order after a reconnect. Seen during token rotate on staging.

omar: interesting, are the payloads identical? or is this a parser/state bug?

lucy: I instrumented sampleapps: sampleapp-js (fetch-based) swallows leading LF and concatenates correctly. sampleapp-py (requests/eventsource) splits differently and throws. sampleapp-go's reader batches small chunks and when resumed it can flush buffers in wrong sequence if last-chunk-id not tracked.

penny: here's a curl -v -N from staging (masked):

```
$ curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer x" "https://staging.redwood.io/s/stream"
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
: keepalive\ndata: {"id":"A","v":1}\n\n\r\n{"id":"B","v":2}\n\n```

penny: JS parser normalizes CRLF and treats the second JSON as new event. python-eventsource lib we use treats the standalone '{' as ill-formed because it expects a leading 'data:' line for every chunk, not bare JSON. go-sdk's chunk-assembler sometimes reorders when multiple small writes are coalesced then re-emitted after reconnect.

omar: TL;DR: parity gap. JS forgiving, py strict, go reassembly bug. we need consistent semantics in our SDKs: prefer canonical SSE framing--server should always send 'data:' lines, and clients should normalize CRLF and trim leading non-printables. also, clients should drop partial event on abort.

lucy: proposed fixes:
- python: switch to fetch-based EventSource polyfill in browsers? not applicable. For py: update eventsource lib wrapper to treat bare JSON chunks as data lines (wrap with implicit 'data: '), and normalize CRLF.
- go: ensure chunk assembler preserves write ordering across reconnects; add last-event-id re-sync.
- js: add metric for repaired_messages so we can see how often we're masking server issues.

penny: i ran a quick matrix: before fixes, on 5k reconnect loops JS errors=0.2%, py errors=4.1% (exceptions), go out-of-order=1.8%. after js normalization + py wrapper + go assembler fix in branch, py exceptions dropped to 0.5% (now repaired), go ordering to 0.05%.

taylor: let's also add explicit test harness in repo: cross-sdk replay that injects CRLF/NUL/fragmented writes and checks final event ordering + parse success. we should fail the build if any SDK diverges.

omar: agree. also add server-side lint: ensure streaming endpoints always emit 'data:' prefixed lines and end with '\n\n'. small server-side change avoids many client fixes. but clients should still be defensive.

penny: opened PRs: js-sdk/patch-crlf-normalize, py-sdk/sse-wrap-bare-json, go-sdk/assembler-fix. CI for all three green. dev-bot: builds passed.

dev-bot: All checks passed on branches: js-sdk (7/7), py-sdk (6/6), go-sdk (5/5) :white_check_mark:

lucy: after merge: backport py and go fixes to 0.9.x branches and add a note to sampleapp README about SDK parity and how to curl -v -N for debugging. taylor: can you add the cross-sdk flapper job to CI?

taylor: yep, will add a Matrix job that spins up lightweight clients and runs the fragmenter harness. scheduling follow-up.

penny: thanks! will monitor repaired_messages metric and open follow-up if any SDK shows >0.2% post-deploy.
